title: Quasi-inequivalence of Thurston representatives of non-conjugate pseudo-Anosov classes in the identity component of the homeomorphism group
author: Lukas Böke
work: Non-orientable surfaces have stably unbounded homeomorphism group
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 4.9 (source label 'thm:main-thing'), a generalisation of Theorem 5.2 of Bowden, Hensel and Webb: two Thurston representatives of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes of a surface which are not conjugate in the mapping class group of the punctured surface are not quasi-equivalent in the identity component of the homeomorphism group. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a genuine argument rather than a citation of the orientable case: it builds quasi-geodesic axes for both representatives simultaneously in the fine curve graph and in the curve graph of the punctured surface, records their quality constants, turns the assumed quasi-equivalence into a sequence of homeomorphisms bringing the boundary points of the two invariant foliations together, uses hyperbolicity of the fine curve graph to confine the images of the axes to bounded neighbourhoods of the other representative's axes, and finally combines the weighted projection proposition with a C^0-small isotopy supported near the punctures to produce a mapping class that contradicts the non-conjugacy hypothesis. The hierarchical hyperbolicity machinery that the argument depends on is retained in full as context, so the counted proof is delivered complete, and the transfer of the orientable theorem to the non-orientable surfaces studied here is research-level geometric topology well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
